questions.question: What is an ecological population?
choices: One species' members in a defined area

questions.question: What does population density measure?
choices: Individuals per unit area or volume

questions.question: What is immigration in ecology?
What is emigration in ecology?
What does carrying capacity describe?
choices: Population size supported over time under given conditions
The greatest count ever observed anywhere
A value unaffected by environmental change

questions.question: Which ideal growth curve is J-shaped?
What is a density-dependent factor?
choices: A factor whose effects vary with crowding
A factor equally strong at every density
A factor determined only by latitude

questions.question: Why does logistic growth slow near carrying capacity?
choices: Resources become more limited per individual

questions.question: Which processes increase population size when acting alone?
Why can drought change carrying capacity?
choices: It changes the definition of species
It forces every individual to migrate
It changes water and food availability

questions.question: How can crowding increase disease transmission?
choices: It can create more contact opportunities
It guarantees all individuals are infected

questions.question: What can age structure help predict?
choices: The exact date of each death
How many individuals are reaching or leaving reproductive ages

questions.question: Why conduct population surveys repeatedly?
choices: To distinguish short-term variation from longer-term trends

questions.question: How can a population briefly exceed carrying capacity?
choices: Reproduction can continue before shortages fully affect survival
An overshoot guarantees unlimited future resources
Populations can change only through migration

questions.question: What limits a simple growth model's predictions?
choices: Assumptions may omit resource changes, movement, or age structure

questions.question: A population starts at 100, has 20 births and 10 deaths, with no migration. What is its final size?
There are 200 fish in 50 hectares. What is their density?
Fifteen individuals immigrate and 25 emigrate, with no births or deaths. What is the net change?
Which event's direct effect is usually density-independent?
One habitat has less usable food and space than another for the same species. What is reasonable, all else equal?
choices: Its carrying capacity must be higher
Resources do not affect carrying capacity
